title: Autoscaler telemetry gap rescue and post-incident action plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-02-17 at ~09:12 UTC we observed sustained throughput degradation for several Dedicated customer pools. Autoscaler metrics stopped emitting scale signals for affected pools which caused nodes to remain undersized for ~47 minutes before manual intervention. This ticket captures the rescue actions taken during the incident, the root-cause and contributing factors, and a prioritized post-incident action plan to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-02-17 09:05 UTC - First alert: token latency SLO miss for pool-p09 reported by Console
2026-02-17 09:12 UTC - Autoscaler health probe for pool-p09 returned stale metrics; scale decision was skipped
2026-02-17 09:25 UTC - Engineering on-call triaged; determined autoscaler had stopped ingesting Prometheus target `pool_metrics` for specific shards
2026-02-17 09:45 UTC - Temporary mitigation: manual reserve nodes allocated to affected pools and request-routing set to circuit-breaker fallback
2026-02-17 09:59 UTC - Hotfix deployed: revert of opaque telemetry sampling change; autoscaler resumed normal decisioning
2026-02-17 10:00-11:00 UTC - Gradual latency recovery observed; full recovery by 10:30 UTC for most pools
2026-02-17 12:00 UTC - Post-incident call and initial notes taken; actions identified
impact: ~120K requests impacted across 7 dedicated pools; peak P95 token latency increased from 180ms to 720ms. No data exfiltration; customer-facing errors were largely 503s due to queue saturation. Several high-usage enterprise customers experienced degradation for up to 47 minutes.
detection_details: Console alerting triggered on request latency SLO violation. Primary detection signal was per-pool P95 latency. Root cause was not immediately obvious because autoscaler control-plane logs showed normal operation but its decision pipeline had an upstream telemetry gap.
root_cause: Primary: a telemetry sampling change merged in runtime-1.22 inadvertently filtered metric labels used by the Dedicated autoscaler (label normalization removed `pool_shard` label for high-cardinality targets). The autoscaler relies on `pool_shard` to map shard-level utilization. Secondary contributors: a recent kube-proxy upgrade changed scrape jitter behaviour, increasing scrape timeouts and creating transient partial scrape failures; and our autoscaler had insufficient defensive handling for missing labels (silent skip instead of degraded decision).
mitigation_steps_taken: Immediate: manual node reservation + routing to lower-tier fallback to protect SLAs
Hotfix: reverted telemetry sampling change in runtime-1.22 (PR #12866) to restore pool_shard labels
Stabilization: temporarily increased autoscaler decision frequency to shorten reaction window during recovery
Post-incident: added temporary synthetic metric to monitor presence of `pool_shard` label for each pool
resolution_summary: After reverting the sampling change and reintroducing the pool_shard label, the autoscaler resumed making scale decisions; added reserved-capacity cushions prevented customer-visible errors from turning into longer outages. Recovery completed within ~47 minutes; no follow-on regressions observed in the 72h monitoring window.
action_items: ENG: Add strict schema validation for critical autoscaler metric labels - owner: Marco Ruiz - estimate: 3
ENG/Telemetry: Implement end-to-end label presence checks in CI (simulate stale scrapes) - owner: Priya Nair - estimate: 5
ENG/Runtime: Add regression test that validates sampling rules do not drop autoscaler labels - owner: Linh Tran - estimate: 3
SRE: Enable a guard that triggers a protective scaling mode when autoscaler telemetry drops below threshold - owner: Ben Turner - estimate: 5
Product: Update customer incident notification template for capacity shortfalls to include expected mitigation and timeframe - owner: Maria Gomez - estimate: 2
Console: Add explicit alert for missing `pool_shard` label with an automated runbook link - owner: Daniel Cho - estimate: 2
acceptance_criteria: CI tests fail if any change in runtime sampling removes `pool_shard` label from autoscaler metrics
Daily dashboard shows label presence ratio >= 99.9% for 30 days post-change
Autoscaler enters protective scaling mode automatically if label presence drops below 95% for 2 consecutive decision windows
Postmortem action items scheduled and started within the next cycle

postmortem_notes: Label hygiene is a high-risk change surface: any sampling/normalization must have an explicit whitelist of labels consumed by downstream control planes
Autoscaler decision logic must degrade into a conservative scaling mode (scale up on missing telemetry) rather than ignore decisions
Observability gaps: we had no discrete alert for missing required labels, only symptom-based alerts (latency). Add direct instrumentation checks.
Release process: require telemetry-owner signoff for any sampling or scrape rule changes that affect production targets
